findings.problem: The same coordinate computation is written out three times: B.repr (c • B i) j = if j = i then c else 0. It is done by `simp only [map_smul, repr_self, smul_single]`, then `by_cases`, then `subst`, then `simp`. The copies are in this theorem, in `f4ShortRootSignedSimpleAdjointMatrix_eq_rootMatrix_map` (Modular/Matrix.lean) and in `f4ShortRootDividedAdjointSquare_basis` (Modular/DividedAction.lean). This theorem also goes backwards. Modular/Matrix.lean already proves the exact statement as the private lemma `f4ShortRootSignedSimpleAdjoint_basis`, and uses it to derive the matrix equality. Here the matrix equality is unpacked entry by entry to re-derive that statement. The divided-square counterpart `f4ShortRootIdealDividedSquareColumn_eq` is a one-line `exact f4ShortRootDividedAdjointSquare_basis k a`, so the two column lemmas are proved asymmetrically.
findings.proposed_change:
1. In Modular/Matrix.lean (or an earlier file), add a lemma `f4ShortRootLieIdealBasis_repr_smul_basis (c : ZMod 2) (i j : Fin 26) : f4ShortRootLieIdealBasis.repr (c • f4ShortRootLieIdealBasis i) j = if j = i then c else 0`. Prove it by `simp only [map_smul, Module.Basis.repr_self, Finsupp.smul_single]`, then the existing `by_cases`/`subst`/`simp` argument, or `Finsupp.single_apply` with `eq_comm`. Use it in the three places that currently inline the block (Matrix.lean around lines 406–416, DividedAction.lean 319–328, and here).
2. Make `f4ShortRootSignedSimpleAdjoint_basis` in Modular/Matrix.lean non-private, like its divided counterpart.
3. Then this theorem becomes `f4ShortRootIdealFirstColumn_eq k a := f4ShortRootSignedSimpleAdjoint_basis k a`, possibly after `unfold f4ShortRootIdealFirstColumn`. It needs the same imports and hypotheses as the divided version. The `ext`/`calc` block and the `rootMatrix_apply` case split here are deleted.
findings.benefit: The basis-coordinate computation lives in one named lemma instead of three copies. The two column lemmas (first order and divided square) get the same one-line proof, which fixes the asymmetry. This file no longer re-derives the sparse-column formula from the matrix equality, which Modular/Matrix.lean proved by going the other way. Future column lemmas, for example further divided powers, can reuse the helper.
